sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Aditya Singh Tomar, learned counsel for the appl  Shri Hemant Sharma, learned counsel for the State.
ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is second application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. (now section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) for grant of bail to the applicant, relating to FIR/Crime No.05/2023, Dated :- 07.02.2023 registered at P.S. - Crime Branch, Indore, District - Indore (M.P.)
for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of IPC and under Sections 34(1), 34(2) and 49-A of Excise Act.
2. The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed on merits vide order dated 12.12.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.50672/2023.

3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that on 06.02.2023, a secret information received by P/S Crime Branch, Indore that present applicant Amit Kumar Jain @ Sonu and co-accused Anand Jatiya, in a rented room, at Samarth Residency, P/S Gandhinagar have brought duplicate items for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26802 2 MCRC-34625-2024 preparation of liquor and are supposed to make and supply it.

The Crime Branch proceeded towards the spot and it was found that the accused persons present applicant and co-accused Anand were present in the Amit Kumar Jain @ Sonu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41647475/
1 aforesaid room.

sentences.text: Present applicant was making bottle caps of Royal Stag by machine and the other accused Anand was packing the bottles in boxes.
There was packaging material spread everywhere in the room.
The accused persons tried to flee away as they saw the police, but failed and were caught by police.

96 bottles of fake Royal Stag poisonous liquor, 10 bottles of spirit of 35L each,
100L of poisonous liquor, 185 quarters country made masala, 73L of plain poisonous liquor,
pressure machine, caps of 612 Royal Stag bottles, 864 empty plastic, 5000 hologram stickers, 1200 hologram stickers, electric weigh machine, 1275 blue caps, 2000 yellow caps, 4800 cover packages of Royal Stag, Alchometer, Hydrometer, Thermometer, sticker 1650, 1220 cover packages of Royal Stag bottles, 2000 wrappers of country-made liquor, 240 wrapper of country-made Masala, 22 empty bottles of Royal Stag, 150 empty quarters of Royal Stag, and other materials, total worth of Rs.5,00,000/- from possession of present applicant Amit and around 33 litres of liquor was recovered from possession of co-accused Anand.
Both the aforesaid accused persons were arrested.
During investigation, it was found that co-accused Santosh Rai and Mohammad Saleem used to supply spirit and raw materials to the accused persons for the preparation of poisonous liquor.
The co- accused persons Santosh Rai and Mohammad Saleem were also arrested.
Accused Mohammad Saleem disclosed that he supplies spirit to the present applicant Amit and co-accused Anand as an agent of Afzal.
The police NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26802 3 MCRC-34625-2024 seized 35L spirit in a plastic can from the accused Mohammad Saleem on 08.02.2023.
Afzal supplies duplicate items to make liquor at low price to present applicant Amit after co-accused Santosh introduced Amit to Afzal.
Packaging items are also present at the home of Santosh as disclosed by him.
Police seized raw materials and packaging articles used to make Royal Stag liquor from the possession of accused Santosh.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused persons submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is submitted that earlier one criminal case of likewise this offence was pending against the applicant before Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Khategaon, District-Dewas which is decided on 03.12.2020 wherein applicant has been acquitted.

Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Khategaon, District-Dewas
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that at present no other criminal case is pending against the applicant.

It is also further submitted that co-accused Anand was granted bail by this Court vide order dated 08.04.2024 in M.Cr.C. No.13167/2024 and the case of the present applicant is identical with the co-accused Anand.
Applicant has completed incarceration of more than one year and six months but till date only 3 prosecution witnesses have been examined before the trial court out of 19 witnesses.
Seizure witnesses Madan Dubey (P.W.-1) and Rajuprasad Dixit (P.W.-2) have not supported the case of the prosecution.
Conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, therefore it is prayed that on the basis of parity applicant be released on bail.
5. On other hand, learned counsel State/non-applicant has objected the prayer and prayed for its rejection.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26802 4 MCRC-34625-2024 6.

Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the custody period of the applicant, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence, without commenting on the Amit Kumar Jain @ Sonu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41647475/
2 merits of the case, the application is allowed.

sentences.text: 7. It is directed that applicant- AMIT KUMAR JAIN @ SONU shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court, for his appearance before the concerned Court regularly on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr.P.C. (now Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023).
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
9. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
